### Observed differences

- The three activities A32, A33 and A34 moved from optional to universal: before, each appeared in roughly half of the cases (about 52 in 100 for A32, 48–49 in 100 for A33 and A34, about once per case when present); in the later window each appears in every case, about once per case. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Before, A32 and the pair A33/A34 were alternatives: A32 co-occurred with A33 in about 1 of 200 cases and with A34 in none, while A33 and A34 co-occurred in about 48 in 100 cases with the order split between them. In the later window all three co-occur in essentially every case, and A33/A34 still occur in both orders (about 50/50). [REL013, REL014, REL015]
- A25's successor changed almost completely: before, about 97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A26; in the later window about 50 in 100 go to A33 and about 48 in 100 to A34, with A26 no longer a direct successor. [DIR001]
- The order around A26 and A28 flipped: before, A26 preceded A33 and A28 preceded A33/A34 in roughly 48 in 100 cases each; in the later window A33 and A34 precede A26 in about 99 in 100 cases and precede A28 in essentially all cases. [REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009]
- Routing around A32 changed: A28 now sends about 99 in 100 of its transitions to A32 (about 51 in 100 before, with the rest split between A33 and A34), A32 still precedes A29 in about 98 in 100 cases, and A33/A34 now lead to A26 (about 48 in 100 each) rather than to A29 (about 54 and 43 in 100 before). [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL010]
- Typical distances changed accordingly: A25→A26 went from adjacent (gap 1 in about 97 in 100 cases) to 3–4 event positions apart; A25→A33 and A25→A34 went from 4–5 positions to 1–2; A33→A29 and A34→A29 went from 1–2 positions to 5. Event positions moved consistently: A26 later (mean about 0.43 to 0.49), A33/A34 earlier (about 0.54 to 0.44), A32 and A29 slightly later. [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG008, LAG009, POS001, POS005, POS006, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the exclusive branch — in which A32 was executed in about half the cases instead of A33 and A34, after A28 — was replaced by a single path in which A33 and A34 (in either order) run immediately after A25 and before A26, and A32 runs between A28 and A29, with all three activities now executed in every case. The order flips are shown directly by the before/after relation profiles, the successor changes by the routing profiles, the distance changes by the gap profiles, and the shift from about half to full participation by the occurrence profiles; the number of qualifying items (37) is far above the roughly 0.64 expected by chance alone, and the completeness of the flips (0 of 200 co-occurrences before versus all 200 after) makes sampling noise an unlikely explanation. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG008, LAG009]

Limitations: the exact placement of A32 between A28 and A29 rests on routing and relation evidence rather than a direct distance measure for that pair; one distance item (A26–A34) rests on a single observation and was not relied on; and the items describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is a shift in the mix of process variants — the later window reflecting one variant that happened to be absent from the 200 earlier traces — although a variant absent from 200 earlier cases yet covering all 200 later cases makes this unlikely. [LAG006, REL013, OCC001]
